slot.brief: A block on a rough horizontal surface is pulled by a force inclined at an angle to the horizontal; ask for the acceleration or the minimum force to just move it (symbolic/numeric).

stem: A block of mass 5 kg lies on a rough horizontal surface with coefficient of friction 0.5. A force of 50 N is applied at an angle of 37 degrees above the horizontal. The acceleration of the block is: (Take g = 10 m/s^2, sin 37 degrees = 0.6, cos 37 degrees = 0.8)
working: N = mg - F sin theta = 5*10 - 50*0.6 = 50 - 30 = 20 N. f = mu N = 0.5*20 = 10 N. Net force = F cos theta - f = 50*0.8 - 10 = 40 - 10 = 30 N. Acceleration a = net force / mass = 30/5 = 6 m/s^2.
solution: The normal reaction is $N=mg-F\sin37^\circ=50-30=20\,\text{N}$, so friction is $f=\mu N=10\,\text{N}$.\n$$a=\frac{F\cos37^\circ-f}{m}=\frac{40-10}{5}=6\,\text{m/s}^2.$$
